isc2.cc.d1.risk-lifecycle: Identify the asset, the threats to it, and the vulnerabilities they could exploit
Assess likelihood x impact and rank it against the other risks
Choose a treatment: mitigate, transfer, avoid or accept
Implement the chosen treatment and verify it
Document the residual risk and have it formally accepted

items_under_review.item: Requiring each engineer to approve change requests with a private key that only they hold
items_under_review.reason: Approving a record with a private key held only by one person is a digital signature that binds the approval to that individual, the textbook CC non-repudiation case; the faint pull toward Authentication (private key as a credential) is outweighed by the act being an approval on a record rather than a login.

items_under_review.item: You report a peer who is selling leaked ISC2 exam questions to candidates
items_under_review.your_answer: Canon IV — advance and protect the profession
items_under_review.reason: The subject is a peer's misconduct undermining the credential and the field's standing, which is Canon IV; it is not about your own honesty (II), no client is involved (III), and there is no public-safety harm (I).

items_under_review.item: You tell a client up front that a specialised cloud engagement is beyond what you are qualified to deliver
items_under_review.your_answer: Canon III — provide diligent and competent service to principals
items_under_review.reason: Rendering only services you are competent and qualified for is guidance under Canon III and the duty exists because of the client relationship, though the 'tell ... up front' framing gives a mild honesty pull toward Canon II that hint 2 addresses.
items_under_review.suggested_fix: Optional: reduce the honesty framing so competence is the clear focus, e.g. 'You decline a client's specialised cloud engagement because it is beyond what you are qualified to deliver.'

items_under_review.item: Implement the chosen treatment and verify it
items_under_review.your_answer: position 4 (after choosing a treatment, before documenting residual risk)
items_under_review.reason: A treatment must be chosen before it can be implemented, and residual risk can only be documented and accepted once the implemented control's actual effect is known.

hints.reason: The 'verify before acting' vs 'evidence checkable later' test correctly separates the MFA and fingerprint items from the two signing items, including the private-key approval.
The organisation-vs-individual-control split cleanly isolates the data-minimisation and erasure items as Privacy without pulling any identity item across.
The 'would you owe this if nobody had hired you' test routes the competence and conflict-of-interest items to III and the rest correctly to I, II or IV; I found no item it misdirects.
It correctly keeps the sales-pitch and unauthorised-scan items in II while moving the honesty-flavoured client-competence disclosure to III and the peer report to IV.
It correctly places identification (asset, threat, vulnerability) before likelihood x impact ranking.

It gives a usable dependency rule (residual risk is measured against the response as implemented, not as planned), which stops a candidate from placing residual-risk acceptance straight after choosing a treatment and forces implement-and-verify first.
